path.description: Path to a JSONL fine-tuning dataset (one example per line).
path.title: Path

kinds.description: Subset of recognizers/entities to run (default: all available).
kinds.title: Kinds

text_fields.description: Top-level field name(s) that hold the training TEXT to scan (e.g. ['source_text'] or ['messages']). null = auto: scan every field but keep only free-text leaves — short whitespace-free strings (tokens, BIO labels, ids, chat roles) are skipped so a tokenized/labelled dataset doesn't run the NER once per token (#1021).
text_fields.title: Text Fields

backend.description: 'auto' (presidio if installed, else regex) | 'regex' | 'regexset' (single-pass re2, [fastpii] extra) | 'presidio' | 'cascade' (regex-in-presidio, ADR-0079).
backend.title: Backend

preset.description: Ready-made PII-scan configuration; individual settings below override it. 'governed' (default) = spaCy NER + regex + secrets — finds names, locations, emails, phones, cards, API keys (best recall; ~7 min/200k rows on a 2-CPU box, ~550 MB). 'logs' = regex + secrets only, NO name/location detection (NER off) — faster and ~200 MB; use for logs, traces, and incident data with no personal names.
preset.title: Preset

ner.description: Detect names & locations (PERSON/LOCATION/ORGANIZATION) with the spaCy model — the PII that has no fixed pattern. Turn OFF for regex + secrets only: much faster and lighter, but names and places are NOT found. Leave ON for training data; off is only safe for structured/log data. null = use the preset's value.
ner.title: Ner

model.description: Language model powering name/location detection (ignored when NER is off). 'sm' = fast, ~550 MB, misses ~1-2% of names (best on a small box); 'lg' = highest recall, ~1.2-1.7 GB, same speed; 'blank' = tokenizer only (no NER). null = use the preset's model.
model.title: Model

n_process.description: CPU workers sharing the detection pass. 0 = auto (all cores) — on a 2-CPU box ~40% faster than a single worker. 1 = single process (lowest RAM, e.g. when the box runs other heavy services). Values above the core count are capped automatically. null = use the preset's value.
n_process.title: N Process

analyze_chunk.description: Rows fed to the detector at once. Larger batches keep the parallel workers busy (needed for 'n_process' to actually help); smaller batches use less memory. ~2048 is a good balance — you rarely need to change it. null = use the preset's value.
analyze_chunk.title: Analyze Chunk

sample_size.description: Reservoir-sample this many rows before checking — a statistically valid estimate for a readiness gate that keeps the scan O(1) in dataset size (the #737 safe cap; presidio-per-row on an unbounded HF dataset can wedge a small box). Set null to scan every row. Deployment/workflow-tunable via PiiScanConfig (ADR-0070).
sample_size.title: Sample Size

max_findings.description: Cap the enumerated `findings` list at this many rows so the REPORT stays bounded on a heavily-PII, >>RAM corpus (#891) — `counts` and `rows_with_pii` remain EXACT (every row is still scanned), only the per-row detail list is capped (`findings_truncated` flags it). 0 = unbounded (small-file convenience).
max_findings.title: Max Findings

secrets_full_scan.description: ADR-0080 P1 — the SECRET tier (AWS/OpenAI/GitHub keys, JWTs, private keys) scans EVERY row with cheap regex, even when NER density is sampled: a rare leaked key would slip past a 1000-row sample ~90% of the time. Merged into `counts` in the gate's blocking vocabulary. Set false only for a pure density estimate with no absolute-blocker guarantee.
secrets_full_scan.title: Secrets Full Scan
